summary: B. R. Gopal (1930–1997) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a Technical Research Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964), Epigraphical Assistant for the Government Epigraphist (attested 1965), and Epigraphist at Epigraphia Carnatica (attested 1974).

Baatr Kitinov works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. in World History from Moscow State University and has served as an Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Baburam Saksena (1897–1989) worked in linguistics and Indology. An advanced student at Banaras Hindu University in 1921, he later served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University circa 1964–1966.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra (b. 1908) studied at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University. A scholar of Indology and archaeology, he served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966), as Government Epigraphist (~1945–1953), and as professor at Panjab University (~1965–1973).

Baiei Henmi (1891–1977) was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1915–1918). He held a post at Tama Art University (~1953–1968) and taught Osamu Takata.

Baihui Wu (1919–2014) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1951), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit (~1956–1962), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–1999).

Baij Nath Puri (1916–1996) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning his M.Litt. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. He was a professor at the University of Lucknow (~1971–1976) and served in UNESCO and the Indian History Congress.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856–1920) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, and Government Law College. He taught at the New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890), both of which he founded.

Bal Krishen Thapar (1921–1995), a historian and archaeologist, studied at University of the Punjab, under Mortimer Wheeler, and at Heidelberg. He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and Chairman of CCRT (1982–1992).
Bala Sahai Shastri worked in the field of Indology. He held posts at Panjab University, serving as an Assistant (attested 1932) and as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1947).
Baliram Shukla is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. At Savitribai Phule Pune University, he has served as Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as Professor (attested 2026).
Balram Shukla (b. 1982) works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Delhi (~2000–2008), where he later became a Professor circa 2013.

Balthasar Bickel (b. 1965) is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Zurich (~1987–1993). He held a post at the University of Leipzig (~2002–2011) and later served on an editorial board at Zurich (~2011).

Bangwei Wang (b. 1950) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After completing his doctoral dissertation at Peking University by 1987, he served there as a professor (attested 2000–2017) and later Boya Retired Professor (attested 2026).

Banikanta Kakati (1894–1952) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, subsequently holding posts as Professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and Department Head and Dean at Gauhati University (1948).

Bapu Deva Sastri (1821–1900) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Sevarama, and Dhundiraja Misra. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara A. Holdrege is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, including Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and Professor (attested 2026).

Barbara E. Ward (1919–1983) was a Sinologist educated at Newnham College, the University of London, and the LSE. She held posts at the University of London, Cambridge (~1973–1978), and visiting professorships at Cornell and CUHK (1978–1982).

Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held research posts at Humboldt University (2011–2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the University of Vienna (attested 2022–2026).

Barbara Harriss-White (b. 1946) works in Indology and related fields. Educated at Newstead Wood School, she held posts at the University of East Anglia (~1979–1989), Queen Elizabeth House (~1990–2011), and the University of Oxford (~1990).
